bug_description.original: The vulnerability occurs when reading BAM files, as the qname is not properly NUL terminated. This can lead to possible invalid reads when printing names.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 165-byte witness is a malformed BAM file whose first alignment record materializes `block_len = 73`, `l_qname = 16`, `n_cigar = 2`, and `l_qseq = 10`. `bam_read1()` therefore computes `l_extranul = 0`, so no alignment-padding byte is available to terminate the qname. It allocates `new_l_data = 41` bytes for the record data, which `sam_realloc_bam_data()` rounds up to a 64-byte heap region, then reads 16 qname bytes that are all non-zero `0xb0` bytes. The vulnerable code never verifies that the last qname byte is `\0` before later exposing `b->data` via `bam_get_qname(b)`. The same record's remaining 25 data bytes are also all non-zero, and its malformed CIGAR decodes to `qlen = 370546198`, which disagrees with `l_qseq = 10`. That mismatch takes the logging path in `bam_read1()`, and `hts_log()` calls `vfprintf(..., "%s", bam_get_qname(b))`. In the reproduced ASan run, no terminator was encountered before the end of the 64-byte heap allocation, so `vfprintf` read the 65th byte in the redzone and AddressSanitizer reported a heap-buffer-overflow read. The fixing patch adds an explicit post-read qname-termination repair immediately after the qname load so a terminator is present even when `l_extranul == 0`.

source.description: First project parser/load step for the vulnerable BAM record. `bam_read1()` reads the first record header from the attacker-controlled stream and materializes the record length and BAM core fields that drive the vulnerable path: `block_len = 73`, `l_qname = 16`, `n_cigar = 2`, and `l_qseq = 10` for the staged witness.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 165-byte BAM-like file. Its first alignment record begins at file offset 15; the 4-byte record length field there is `0x49` (`73`), and the following 32-byte BAM core header yields `l_qname = 16`, `n_cigar = 2`, and `l_qseq = 10` when parsed by this code.

tainted_value_origin.description: The first concrete vulnerability-relevant values are the parsed BAM core fields. `l_qname = 16` determines the qname read length and, because it is 4-byte aligned, causes `l_extranul` to become zero. `n_cigar = 2` and `l_qseq = 10` later make the CIGAR/query-length sanity check reach the logging path.

sink.description: Closest project sink to the ASan crash. `vfprintf` consumes the `%s` argument supplied by `bam_read1()` and scans the unterminated `bam_get_qname(b)` pointer until it crosses the 64-byte heap allocation for `b->data`, producing the reproduced heap-buffer-overflow read.

root_cause.description: Root cause. After reading `c->l_qname` bytes of qname data into `b->data`, the vulnerable code never checks whether `b->data[c->l_qname - 1]` is `\0` before the record is later exposed via `bam_get_qname(b)`. The fixing patch inserts exactly that missing post-read validation and repair immediately after this statement.

parser_admitted.condition: For the staged first record, `((2 << 2) + 16 + 0 + ((10 + 1) >> 1) + 10) = 39`, which is `<= new_l_data = 41`, so the malformed record passes `bam_read1()`'s size checks and reaches the qname-loading code despite lacking a terminating NUL.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzz harness wraps the staged `poc` bytes in an `htsFile`, recognizes sequence data, and routes the stream into the SAM/BAM viewing path.
The viewer allocates one `bam1_t` record and iterates `sam_read1()` over the attacker-controlled input.
For BAM input, `sam_read1()` dispatches the next record to `bam_read1()` without additional qname validation.

The first BAM record is accepted by the size checks, loaded into `b->data` with `l_qname = 16` and `l_extranul = 0`, and then the malformed CIGAR/query-length mismatch takes the error-log path that formats `bam_get_qname(b)` as `%s`.
`hts_log()` forwards that unterminated qname pointer to `vfprintf`, which scans past the 64-byte heap allocation and triggers the reproduced ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: Reads the first BAM alignment header from the attacker-controlled stream and materializes the record values that drive the vulnerable path. Static parsing of the staged witness yields `block_len = 73`, `l_qname = 16`, `n_cigar = 2`, and `l_qseq = 10` for this first record.

Derives how many alignment-padding NUL bytes can follow the qname. Because the witness sets `l_qname = 16` and `16 % 4 == 0`, this computes `l_extranul = 0`, so the record has no spare padding byte that could incidentally terminate an unterminated qname.

fine_trace.var: block_len, new_l_data, c->n_cigar, c->l_qname, c->l_extranul, c->l_qseq
fine_trace.note: Computes the logical size of the record payload and checks that the parsed BAM lengths are self-consistent. With `block_len = 73` from step 1 and `l_extranul = 0` from step 2, `new_l_data = 41`; the structural guard also passes because the parsed components require 39 bytes, so the malformed record is accepted instead of rejected.

Allocates storage for the record payload and records the logical data length. `new_l_data` is 41, and `sam_realloc_bam_data()` rounds that request up with `kroundup32`, matching ASan's report that `b->data` points to a 64-byte heap region.

Reads the qname bytes into the start of `b->data`. For the witness, the 16 qname bytes are all `0xb0`, so `b->data[15]` is not `\0`. The vulnerable code still performs no post-read termination check here, leaving `bam_get_qname(b)` unterminated from the moment these bytes are stored.

Completes the record payload after the qname. Because `l_extranul = 0`, the padding loop writes no NUL byte and `c->l_qname` stays 16; the subsequent read appends the remaining 25 attacker-controlled bytes of the record. In the staged witness those 25 bytes are also all non-zero, so the entire 41-byte logical record buffer contains no terminator.

Decodes the query length implied by the record's malformed CIGAR words. The staged record stores two CIGAR entries `0xb0b0b0b0`, so `bam_cigar2rqlens()` derives `qlen = 370546198`, far larger than the parsed `l_qseq = 10`.

The sanity-check predicate that gates the error log evaluates true for the witness: `c->l_qseq > 0` (`10 > 0`), the record is not flagged unmapped, and the derived `qlen` from step 7 does not equal `c->l_qseq`. This takes execution into the logging branch that formats the qname as a C string.

fine_trace.code:
hts_log_error("CIGAR and query sequence lengths differ for %s",
        bam_get_qname(b));
fine_trace.note: Hands the qname to the logger as a `%s` argument. `bam_get_qname(b)` is the macro `(char *)(b)->data`, so this passes the start of the unterminated record buffer from steps 5-6 directly to the formatting code with C-string semantics.

ASan sink. `vfprintf` processes the `%s` argument from step 9 and keeps scanning the `bam_get_qname(b)` pointer for a terminating NUL. In the reproduced run, the scan traversed the entire 64-byte heap allocation for `b->data` without finding one and then read the 65th byte at the right redzone, producing the reported `READ of size 65` heap-buffer-overflow.

allocation_context.note: The crashing string pointer lives in `b->data`, which is allocated by `realloc_bam_data(b, new_l_data)` at this call site. ASan reports the resulting heap object as a 64-byte region.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch is source-grounded to this bug: it adds `fixup_missing_qname_nul()` and inserts `if (b->data[c->l_qname - 1] != '\0') { ... }` immediately after the qname read at `sam.c:578`, exactly where the vulnerable trace leaves `bam_get_qname(b)` unterminated. Stage 01 did not execute a fixed build for this sample, so `patch_resolves` remains false even though the patch matches the traced root cause.

format.name: BAM file consumed by htslib's SAM/BAM reader through hts_open_fuzzer
format.contract: A BAM input whose first alignment record passes `bam_read1()`'s structural size checks, sets `l_qname = 16` so `l_extranul == 0`, stores 16 qname bytes with no `\0`, leaves the remaining 25 bytes of that same record non-zero, and makes the parsed CIGAR disagree with `l_qseq` so `bam_read1()` executes `hts_log_error(..., bam_get_qname(b))`. The staged 165-byte witness satisfies that exact contract with `block_len = 73`, qname bytes `0xb0 * 16`, and two malformed CIGAR words `0xb0b0b0b0`, yielding `qlen = 370546198` versus `l_qseq = 10`.
